newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ATHERTON APPEALS FOR WIVES TO STAY AT HOME.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ATHERTON APPEALS FOR WIVES TO STAY AT HOME.

text.p: England cricket captain Mike Atherton has appealed to his squad to keep wives and girlfriends away from the tour of Zimbabwe and New Zealand.
But several players are still believed to be planning to fly in their partners during the 14-week tour, which starts on November 25 and includes the Christmas and New Year period.
Atherton and England's management held a team meeting during a training trip to Portugal this week to try to settle the issue.
Atherton said on Thursday: "We have had a chat about it and there were some strong views aired. We have tried to persuade the players we would like, in this instance, families to stay at home.
"But there is no clause saying players will be disciplined if wives come out. I don't, however, expect to see any."

Atherton added: "It's important from the players' point of view that the structure of tours is looked into. Australia and the West Indies will always be long trips but others should perhaps be a bit shorter."
More than half of England's 15-man squad are married, with seven players having small children.
